work.title: فمن خلق الله؟

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Section opens: modern cosmology is presented as confirmation of the philosophical proof of created time and space; opposition to material eternity frames the unit.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Section title, opening program, confirmation relation, printed page number.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Big Bang introduced as origination of space and time, with figurative-explosion caveat; heat death and early Einstein/Friedmann/Slipher history.
Slipher/Hubble expansion history, Lemaître and the primeval-atom proposal, and the hot early state.
Gamow, microwave-background discovery and later confirmation, with cited testimony; transition to rival explanations.
Steady-state continuous matter creation contrasted with Big Bang; alleged lack of verification and observational objections begin.
Remaining observational/explanatory objections to steady state and reported preference for the Big Bang based on fewer parameters.
Evidence inventory introduced as most of Hugh Ross's thirty items; item 1 on microwave-background existence and temperature.
Evidence items 2–6: background spectrum, cooling, uniformity, photon/baryon ratio, and thermal variations.
Evidence items 7–11: fluctuation spectrum, expansion rate, orbits, life, and helium.
Evidence items 12–16: deuterium, lithium, general relativity, a conditionally stated Hawking–Penrose theorem, energy density.
Evidence items 17–21 begin: stellar/galactic ages, crowding and morphology, ordinary/exotic matter ratio.
Item 21 concludes; items 22–25 cover light elements in old stars, stellar populations, compact objects, and cluster evolution.
Items 26–27 conclude Ross-derived inventory; section changes from evidence list to scientist testimony.
Reported broad acceptance of Big Bang; polemical claim that materialist/atheist commitments resist the scientific findings.
Reports about Einstein, Eddington, Wilson, Sandage, and Hoyle used to illustrate philosophical resistance or conversion.
Hoyle quotation concludes; Sciama's change of view and Isham's interpretation of motivations.
Isham conclusion, Maddox and later reports; footnote explains why the testimony section is extensive: theological import of Big Bang.
Objection that Big Bang may fail; response begins by distinguishing scientific theory from unsupported conjecture.
Theory response concludes; multiple purportedly independent grounds for a cosmic beginning introduced; second law begins.
Second-law argument explicitly uses assumptions about a closed material cosmos and energy depletion over time.
Davies on irreversibility/equilibrium; generalized-second-law/quantum-cosmology response begins.
Quantum response concludes; relativity and BGV introduced broadly; expansion proposed as a ground beyond the Big Bang model.
Positive-expansion formulation of BGV, incompleteness language, and conclusion against eternity; Olbers paradox begins.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Positive-expansion condition, incompleteness wording, subsequent anti-eternity conclusion, footnote placement.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Olbers paradox with spatial/temporal infinity assumptions; cumulative-evidence response and Jastrow reply to future-science objection begin.
Jastrow reply concludes; broad model distinguished from subsidiary theories; inflation presented as internal problem-solving.
Cumulative evidence and predictive success; reported statements from Davies, Stenger, Burnham, Rees.
Rees continuation; Cannon, Will, ESA/Planck confirmations reported.
Planck confirmation concludes; alternatives section begins, with explicit acknowledgment of reliance on Craig; cyclic model introduced.
Cyclic model: rational objection to infinitely many past cycles plus empirical, entropy, density, and mechanism objections.
Cyclic objections finish, including fine adjustment; finite past contrasted with infinite future; eternal/chaotic inflation introduced.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Conditional concession to cyclic history and explicit future/past infinity asymmetry; transition to inflation.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Eternal inflation: testability criticism, Borde–Vilenkin beginning claim, reported Linde response.
Later inflation criticism; string-related pre-Big-Bang model and objections involving old/merged black holes and equilibrium.
Ekpyrotic/cyclic brane scenario; rational infinity, internal issues, design, and BGV objections.
Reported Steinhardt beginning qualification; vacuum-fluctuation model explicitly permits our universe to begin without an absolute beginning; objections start.
Vacuum objection concludes with inference from eternal initial energy to eternal products; Hartle–Hawking imaginary/real time distinction begins.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Eternal-energy/products wording; Hartle–Hawking section and imaginary/real-time distinction.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Imaginary time treated as mathematical device; smooth beginning without a singular first point distinguished from real history.
Hartle–Hawking conclusion: beginning without singularity, possible endless future; separate motionless-eternal-cosmos objection begins with relational account of time.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Beginning without singularity and endless future; transition to motionless-eternal case.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Motionless-eternal scenario rejected by causal and physical arguments; ontological precedence stated; active quantum vacuum distinguished from no motion; recap begins.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Ontological precedence, no-motion/time relation, and distinction from active quantum vacuum.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Recap items 1–2: strong claim of scientific origination evidence and resilience of the Big Bang.
Item 2 concludes; item 3 explicitly distinguishes Big Bang history from absolute beginning; item 4 categorizes eternal alternatives.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Explicit local-versus-absolute-beginning distinction and adjacent recap structure.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Wider-universe/BGV objection and Mithani–Vilenkin report; item 5 on speculative pre-Planck alternatives and evidential limits.
Reported Jastrow/Guth limits; item 6 demands historical traces and mechanisms and notes missing quantum-gravity theory.
Item 6 concludes; item 7 gives design/fine-tuning fallback for proposed eternal universes.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Separate design/fine-tuning fallback for proposed eternal models.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Items 8–9: origination/fine-balance summary and rational/scientific convergence; boxed conclusion contains a visually verified apparent wording reversal.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Boxed wording anomaly confirmed as printed, not extraction error; convergence claim.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Two-option framing qualified by recognition that eternity does not logically exclude a creator for many ancient philosophers; future-science objection starts.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Parenthetical qualification that eternity need not logically deny a creator; adjacent Islamic-creation claim.

pages.page_summary_paraphrase: Future-science reply finishes; last point expressly retains an independently conclusive rational proof irrespective of scientific developments.
pages.visual_check_purpose: Final assertion of conclusive rational proof independent of scientific developments.
